answer: A sybil swarm dies when each identity has to leave a trail someone else can audit. The design leans on honeypot tasks with known-bad answers, capped per identity per epoch, auditors are drawn from a rotating pool. Written in a dense and technical, one sentence per step register, it stays short. By the horizon of the epoch the only identities still standing are the ones whose work held up. The voyage is public, so padding it with copies shows up as duplicated leaves on the island.
